title: Fix native hook admission, encrypted output and Codex resume
body:
This PR moves ordinary hook enforcement to the native runtime, handles encrypted Pi/OMP post-tool output on POSIX, and defers daemon manager imports until explicit access. It also carries the reviewed first-generation admission, Windows private-file replacement, risk-reuse and Codex continuation changes described below.

Current source is `b222318cca2811ac7ae90c7364e2ec6d0a10651f`, tree `ef0c0b8abb8144ed010b4c23c05a2dc70f20c354`, with sole parent `4001185e4f39cad51fd5eab314bf02b86b8a1674`. The latest commit changes only the AES known-answer test and one exact historical Gitleaks fingerprint. Product runtime and workflow bytes are unchanged from that parent. The normal CI merge build is `6aa63accf753de56aef380bdf59710a031973bfa`, with the same tree.

## Resulting behavior

- **Encrypted post-tool output:** Pi and OMP can provide large post-tool output through their existing encrypted reference. On POSIX, Rust opens the bounded private file without following links, verifies ownership, modes, file identity, hash and AES-256-GCM authentication, validates the inner event and metadata, and evaluates the actual content under the original absolute deadline. The receipt retains the outer request commitment and reference kind. Windows encrypted references remain unsupported.
- **Daemon imports:** importing lightweight daemon surfaces no longer eagerly imports the seven manager exports. Explicit access still returns the original function, with shared state initialized before use. All 11 public exports, normal imports, reload, directory listing and monkeypatch behavior have controls. Manager import errors and side effects now occur on first access; direct inspection of the package dictionary can observe unresolved names.
- **First-generation admission:** a fully observed, stable empty command namespace can publish its initial native generation. Unknown, partial, symlink/nonregular or subsequently changed authority remains refused.
- **Windows private-file replacement:** eligible Windows systems use the reviewed POSIX replacement capability while retaining OS error semantics and private-file safety checks.
- **Risk reuse:** unchanged exact request inputs reuse category/signal work. Input, authority, catalog or implementation changes invalidate reuse, including pending approvals and the final deadline fence.
- **Codex approval resume:** browser resume consumes the same two root transport timeout hints as initial HTTP ingress, allowing native revalidation to see the original committed request. Nested input, source/correlation identity, signed approval, current policy, deadlines and replay checks remain binding.
- **Response contracts:** current Cline, auxiliary-event and registration-roster fixtures capture JSON/stdout/stderr/exit behavior for mode/posture, native misses, integrity/size failures, permissions and lifecycle events. Modeled edges are explicit, and the SLO explanation matches its executable predicates.

## Validation

Root verified the complete 4,800-file current tree against GitHub, with exactly two changed files from the parent. The public AES test key now constructs the known sequence 0–31 before encoding it; nonce, ciphertext, payload and assertions retain the same vector. The Gitleaks exception identifies only the original finding's commit, path, rule and line. Pinned Gitleaks 8.24.2 scanned all 1,356 commits from the actual PR base to the current head with zero findings; negative controls still detect the vector at a new commit on the same or a different path. The exact current test passed Rust 1.88 formatting and one collected/one passed known-answer case in [35534312783](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35534312783).

The encrypted-reference source cohort [35530113949](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35530113949) passed **43/43 controls on Linux x86_64, Mac ARM and Mac Intel**, including all 23 new crypto, private-file, bounds, identity, metadata, deadline and content cases, with zero ignored functional cases. Locked, all-target, all-feature Clippy with warnings denied and Rust 1.88 formatting passed. The earlier fixture failure and its correction remain retained; production bytes were unchanged between those cohorts.

The lazy-import candidate passed **393 cases with three existing Windows-only skips**, covering 396 unique cases. Ruff, formatting and diff checks passed; full source typing reported zero errors and 30,183 warnings across 1,434 files. A reviewed data reader reconciled the original wrapper's XML-order failure against actual successful pytest output without rerunning tests. The parent also passed its original Rust workspace census: **341 passed, six explicitly ignored diagnostics, zero failures across 347 unique cases in 18 suites**. All seven existing source gates passed against authentic base ancestry and the exact candidate tree.

| Actual run or evidence | Verified outcome | Scope and remaining limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current native workflow [35534837418](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35534837418) | All four platforms passed; Linux completed at 20:47:37 UTC on 2026-09-20 and the strict artifact collector passed at 20:48:04 UTC. Main CI, security gates and daemon-edge jobs also passed. | Current b222 source and matching 6aa63 merge tree. Final full workflow/check census and the newly uploaded Linux/aggregate artifact bytes are being reconciled. |
| Current Windows | 149 source passes/three POSIX skips; 53 mandatory cases, 90 child frames, 18 Unicode pairs and 21 accepted/processed native deliveries with empty error maps. Original archives and corrected exact raw bytes passed independent review. | The parent’s 20/21 normal result and earlier journal/SQLite failures remain retained and unexplained. |
| Current Macs | Each platform passed 14 ordinary gates and all 21 native/receipt deliveries, including four inline OMP cases and two Claude post-tool smoke cases. Original archives, wheel RECORD and source joins passed independent review. | c16 p95: ARM 437.028 ms; Intel 794.502 ms, against the ordinary 1,000 ms gate. These do not establish the original 50/100/200 ms targets. |
| Installed Pi/OMP encrypted callbacks [35535394779](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35535394779) | All three POSIX platforms passed 162 source controls, ten offered/returned native callbacks, six encrypted post-tool evaluations, ten distinct exact committed receipts and contained cleanup. | Isolated fixture successor using authentic parent 400/37fd wheels. Clean output preserves the actual default warn policy; tail-secret and changed-content cases block. Original failed fixture and source identities are retained. Independent final review reproduced all three original results, all 48 archive members and all 30 complete receipt joins without rerun. Windows encrypted references remain unsupported. |
| Parent Linux soak [35531198716](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35531198716) | 100,000 requests/responses, 250,000 receipts, zero errors; p95 536.86 ms, RSS growth 4.6016%. Original archive and source joins verified. | Parent 400/37fd identity and ordinary 4,500 ms gate. Its strict collector was skipped after other platform failures. |
| Codex continuation [35528764054](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35528764054) | Each POSIX platform passed 90 source controls and one original continuation, with durable exact approval, two native Review evaluations and a fresh completed allow delivered through the suspended response. | Retains a5fd package identity and the finite original scenario. General native approval consumption and the wider lifecycle matrix remain separate. |
| Functional risk reuse [35519707612](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35519707612) | Eight lanes passed all 13 mandatory positive and 49 approval cases; ten direct RSP099 cases passed. | Exact unchanged product providers; original e440 execution retained. |
| Ollama [35523481186](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35523481186) | All 22 cases and 22 durable receipts passed on each POSIX platform. | Authenticated policy review using its actual historical packages. |
| Cline Intel [35531647232](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35531647232) | All four cases have native, receipt and context joins; both post-tool nested calls return normally. | Both pre-tool nested calls time out at the original nine-second limit. The outer fallback's exit zero does not establish delivery of the native verdict. A bounded worker-process observation change is under review. |
| First-admission constructor diagnostic [35531826728](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35531826728) | The original first reply was discarded and its ACK withheld as intended; retained frames locate time within actual startup stages. | Caller-visible readiness still misses the unchanged 400 ms limit, before a recovered request/receipt. The observed 49.689146 ms post-worker interval includes multiple operations and scheduling; it is not a CPU or leaf-function measurement. |
| Mac recovery [35534417441](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/actions/runs/35534417441) | The exact original selector and stop passed; independent review verified archive, source, frame and cleanup joins. | Fresh nonreproduction of the parent failure. Historical cause remains unresolved; the diagnostic binary has runner hash provenance but was not uploaded. |

The parent’s terminal census was 172 successful checks, 20 skipped and four failures (Windows delivery count, Mac recovery, Gitleaks and rate-limited Kilo advisory). Its 29 successful normal workflows, three failed workflows and skipped aggregate collector are preserved. Current-head successes do not rewrite that record.

## Original PRD and completion status

The original 144 task objects and 119 catalog entries remain immutable. The latest published overlay records **80 DONE, 25 OPEN, 29 BLOCKED and 10 DEFERRED**, with current own-scope acceptance for **RSP001/006/007/013/014/015/022/047/099/100/120/133**. Newly accepted RSP007 is the actual registered launcher measurement mechanism, RSP047 is the source-layer correctness cohort, and RSP120 is the documented extension inventory and compatibility boundary. Measurement acceptance does not imply passing latency; historical RSP119 component support does not close its RSP118/010 dependencies or establish execution at the current head.

Remaining work includes admission of the newly completed current-head Linux and aggregate artifact bytes; the full original route, workspace, external-permission and lifecycle matrices; Cline Intel normal pre-tool return; caller-visible first-admission readiness; measured Python import benefit; original performance, offered-load and descendant-resource qualification; and signed/version-bound release, updater, rollback and canary qualification. The original 50/100/200 ms limits, relative-benefit thresholds, populations and full-descendant requirements remain unchanged. Stopped E/F campaigns and completed historical populations cannot be replayed or pooled to fill gaps.

The published [completion checkpoint](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/tree/9b7f26d1e1465261bb248a3b66de39ef4a3ddd8a/review-evidence/2026-09-19/pr2974-completion/addenda/20260920T202000Z-current400-scoped-acceptance) preserves all 12,718 prior leaves and adds 1,538 files, for **14,256 verified leaves**. It includes the current source publication, parent terminal outcomes, scoped acceptance decisions and original diagnostic records. Results completed after its stated cutoff will be added in a successor checkpoint.

The latest formal-review census has 51 COMMENTED reviews and zero approvals; the preceding thread census had all 59 resolved. No eligible CODEOWNER/last-push approval is present. The PR remains open, mergeable and blocked. Full PRD completion and release readiness remain open.
